text:
sam-docs: FYI I opened a docs PR to add runtime profile guidance and a small SDK snippet for the new Deckard-13B variants: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pull/1122. Can someone sanity-check limits and the sample?

anna-docs: Looking now. PR mentions the quant variant default seq=4096 but also says high-memory supports 8192. Do we have consensus on wording? Customers get confused if both numbers appear without context.

mike-eng: Short answer: default safe limit for q4_k_m is 4096. The runtime exposes named profiles; the `high-memory` profile enables a larger KV allocation and has been validated up to 8192 on orion-class GPUs. We should call out both but label them clearly (default vs profile-enabled).

lucy-devex: Also found a stale link in deckard-13b.md pointing to `#runtime-profiles` anchor. The docs site renamed that section to `#profiles`. Link-checker failed.

ci-bot: link-checker: 1 failure  sources/docs/model-catalog/deckard-13b.md: anchor '#runtime-profiles' not found.

sam-docs: I'll update the anchor and add a one-line note: "Quantized variants: default sequence limit 4096; request `profile='high-memory'` to opt into up to 8192 (hardware permitting)." Also planning to include a v2 SDK snippet.

anna-docs: For the snippet, can we use the v2 client shape? Example idea:
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('RW_KEY'))
resp = client.generate(model='deckard-13b-q4_k_m', input='Summarize...', profile='high-memory')
print(resp.text)
```
That demonstrates the `profile` param.

mike-eng: Note: in some older SDK versions the param was `runtime_profile`. Use `profile` to match docs. Also add a short comment showing swapping to `deckard-13b-fp16` for latency-sensitive workloads.

lucy-devex: Agreed. I'll fix the broken anchor to `#profiles` and update the internal link. Also suggest a fallback sentence: if the requested profile is unavailable the router may fallback to a compatible variant or different region (potentially higher latency).

sam-docs: Added the fallback note and linked to the routing policies doc. Kept the language customer-facing and concise.

anna-docs: Can we include a tiny indicative benchmark note? Nothing normative, just ballpark numbers: e.g., on orion-x GPUs, deckard-13b-q4_k_m ~35 tok/s @ seq=2048 batch=1; profile=high-memory gives ~18 tok/s @ seq=8192. Add a clear disclaimer that results vary by hardware/config.

mike-eng: That sounds fine. Make it a footnote and include the testing conditions (batch=1, beam=1).

sam-docs: Done  added a benchmark footnote with conditions and link to the runbook. Also updated the SDK snippet to show both q4 and fp16 variants in comments.

lucy-devex: Two tiny copy edits: simplify the fallback sentence and remove passive voice in the profile paragraph. Also opened a follow-up ticket to sweep older model cards for the old anchor names.

ci-bot: pr-check: doc-lint passed, link-checker passed.

anna-docs: Approved.

sam-docs: Merged. I'll watch the integration and customer feedback channel. Thanks all! :rocket:

mike-eng: One post-merge note: ops asked that we mention the policy name used by the router when preferring profiles (policy: `prefer-profile`). Could add a short parenthetical so oncall can quickly find it.

sam-docs: Added a parenthetical link to the routing doc and the policy name. Thanks.
